$comment: LANE-O (D-LK-EXTERN-DATA-IMPORT, the PE half): the source-level extern-DATA-import RUN witness on Windows, in PLAIN STANDARD C. A bare `extern unsigned char *_mbcasemap;` (ISO/IEC 9899:2024 6.7.1 `declarator`, no initializer, no invented library clause) lowers to HIR ExternGlobal; the shipped-descriptor corpus -- now the SINGLE owner of realization since `externLibraryByFormat` was removed from c.lang.json -- supplies the library from ctype.json's per-format map (pe: ucrtbase.dll); the row survives the LK11 merge as ExternImport{isData} and binds per the pe64 exec format's declared `dataImportBinding: "got-indirect"` (PE `__imp_` semantics: the loader fills the extern's .idata IAT SLOT with the imported OBJECT's address; symbolVa[dataExtern] = the slot VA; NO `FF 25` thunk for data) -> MIR->LIR lea-of-slot + deref, then the C-level load of a `ptr` object reads the pointer's VALUE. * RENAMED from extern_data_import_msvcrt, which is closing verdict (3) of [[D-CONFIG-NO-DESCRIPTOR-FOR-SETLOCALE-FMODE-ENVIRON]]: the old name spelled the LEGACY CRT into a path that no shippedLibs grep and no runtimeLibraries check would ever see, while the arc was migrating pe to UCRT. Both corpus harnesses discover by walking the tree (integrated_tests/runner.cpp `fs::directory_iterator`; tests/examples registers at cmake-configure time via `file(GLOB_RECURSE)`), so the rename needs a cmake RECONFIGURE but no manifest-list edit -- verified, the only in-tree references to the old name were registry prose. * WHY THE SUBJECT CHANGED WITH IT: the predecessor declared `extern int _fmode;` / `extern char **_environ;`, and neither can be an extern-DATA witness on UCRT. MEASURED 2026-08-10 on two concurring instruments (GNU objdump 2.42 `-p`, MSVC dumpbin 14.44.35207 `-exports`) over all 2,484 exports of the live C:/Windows/System32/ucrtbase.dll 10.0.26100.8875: `_fmode` and `_environ` are BOTH ABSENT; UCRT publishes them ONLY via `__p__fmode` (ordinal 88) and `__p__environ` (ordinal 87), which is exactly what ucrt/stdlib.h:255 and :1171 themselves do. They now ship as pe-gated MACROS onto those accessors from stdlib.json and are reached by `#include <stdlib.h>` with NO extern at all -- witnessed by shipped_fmode_environ_pe. Under [[D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT]] a `kind: object` row for either would break the LOAD of every binary that touched it, which the registry row already recorded as PERMANENT for pe. * THE NEW SUBJECT: `_mbcasemap`, one of exactly TWO non-code exports in the whole ucrtbase image (the other is `_wctype`, .rdata, declared in no ucrt header) -- ordinal 527, RVA 0x001397E0, inside `.data` (RVA 0x138000..0x13A623) whose section flags are 0xC0000040 = Initialized Data READ WRITE, which is what makes the store-and-restore leg legal; ALSO an msvcrt.dll export (ordinal 520), so the row survives a revert of the CRT flip. Ships from ctype.json as a pe-gated `kind: object` row -- THE FIRST `kind: object` row the pe axis has ever had (the other seven in the corpus are elf/macho: stdio's stdout/stderr/stdin + __std{in,out,err}p, unistd's __environ). *** IT IS TYPED `ptr<u8>`, NOT AN ARRAY, AND THAT IS A MEASURED REFUTATION OF THE OBVIOUS SHAPE. ucrt/mbctype.h:30 declares `extern unsigned char _mbcasemap[];`, so an array looks faithful. THE UCRT EXPORT IS NOT AN ARRAY: MEASURED by native probe (cl 14.44 /MD, two runs) the 8 bytes AT the export are a POINTER, 0x00007FF85DB28730, BYTE-EQUAL to `__p__mbcasemap()`'s return on the same run, while the export's OWN address is 0x00007FF85DB297E0 (the two differ, so the accessor is not &_mbcasemap); the qword at export+8 is a second pointer exactly +0x100 away, i.e. a POINTER TABLE; and the 256 bytes at the pointed-to address are a real case map, 125 of 256 nonzero. THE MATCHED CONTROL SETTLES IT: legacy msvcrt.dll's `_mbcasemap` (ordinal 520, RVA 0x9E400) IS the table itself with the SAME 125-of-256 population -- the CRT changed the export's SHAPE from array to pointer and the SDK header's direct-declaration arm still describes the msvcrt shape ([[D-FFI-UCRT-HEADER-DECLARES-MBCASEMAP-AS-ARRAY]]). ! AND THE WRONG SHAPE WOULD HAVE SHIPPED SILENTLY, which is the `environ` class exactly -- MEASURED BY EXERCISING THE ARM, not reasoned about: declaring `extern unsigned char _mbcasemap[];` in main.c COMPILES rc=0 with ZERO diagnostics and RUNS to exit 4, caught by the agreement check and by nothing else. Mechanism: got-indirect derefs the slot to the OBJECT's address and an array reference decays THERE via Gep(...,0) (src/lir/lowering/mir_to_lir.cpp:4726-4748 + src/mir/lowering/hir_to_mir.cpp:3245-3264), so `_mbcasemap[0]` reads the first byte of the POINTER (measured 0x30) instead of the case map's first byte (measured 0x00), while a `ptr` object takes the second, C-level load and yields the pointer's VALUE. ! THE DECIDING SURFACE IS THE SOURCE DECLARATOR, NOT THE ROW'S SIGNATURE, and that distinction is worth stating precisely because the natural phrasing blames the wrong owner: realization hands over only the LIBRARY (semantic_analyzer.cpp:14329-14334 drops `real.isFunction`; `CorpusSymbolRow::isObject` is written and never read), so nothing compares a shipped row's `kind` or type against the declaration ⇒ [[D-FFI-SHIPPED-ROW-KIND-NOT-CROSSCHECKED-AGAINST-DECLARATOR]]. The row's type still matters for two non-checking reasons: it is a STATEMENT ABOUT THE OBJECT that readers and future `#include` consumers will believe, and the array form is not even spellable -- src/hir/hir_text.cpp:2022-2024 makes `arr<`'s comma and extent MANDATORY, so a bound would have to be INVENTED. REAL MSVC IS WORSE HERE: linking that same SDK bare-array declaration with cl /MD bound `_mbcasemap` to an IAT SLOT IN THE PROGRAM'S OWN IMAGE (0x00007FF6628530C8, holding the export address) so `_mbcasemap[0]` read 0xE0 -- the low byte of the export's address -- i.e. MSVC's auto-import of data without __declspec(dllimport) is TWO indirections off. DSS is one better because it derefs the slot, and correct only once the row's type matches the object. ** THE LADDER ASSERTS AN AGREEMENT, NOT A MAGIC VALUE, and that is the deliberate improvement over the predecessor, which pinned `_fmode == 0` -- a CRT-version fact that reads IDENTICALLY to an unfilled slot, i.e. a layer that could pass for the wrong reason. The oracle here is `__p__mbcasemap()`, UCRT's OWN accessor for the same state (ordinal 89, RVA 0x000C1D00, MEASURED on both instruments), reached as a separate FUNCTION import, so no address, byte value or count is ever asserted and the pin is host-, locale- and CRT-version-independent: exit 2 = the data import reads 0 (dead/unfilled slot, or dataImportBinding dropped); exit 3 = the ACCESSOR returned 0, guarding the oracle BEFORE exit 4 trusts it so a broken oracle cannot manufacture a pass; exit 4 = THE AGREEMENT CHECK, which discriminates every wrong-binding class at once -- one indirection short (bare lea, no deref) returns the export's own address 0x...97E0 instead of its contents 0x...8730, a thunk-VA bind returns `FF 25`-derived bytes, a stale duplicate disagrees; exit 5 = the case map must hold at least ONE nonzero byte in 0..255 (a live table, not zero-fill -- only EXISTENCE is asserted, never the count, because 125 is a codepage fact); exit 6/7 = store a sentinel THROUGH the data import and read it back through the ACCESSOR's pointer, then restore and re-check, proving the two paths reach the SAME LIVE memory rather than agreeing on a stale address, and that the store lands somewhere writable (a thunk-VA binding puts it in R-X .text -> 0xC0000005, never 42). Index 0 is the NUL character's case map, so the write is inert and the restore is byte-exact. RED-ON-DISABLE: drop `dataImportBinding` from pe64-x86_64-windows-exec.format.json -> K_FormatLacksImportSupport at compile time (the pre-c149 wall); un-ship ctype.json's `_mbcasemap` row -> honest K_SymbolUndefined at link (src/link/linker.cpp:174); retype the SOURCE DECLARATOR to `extern unsigned char _mbcasemap[];` -> exit 4, a RUN failure with NO diagnostic, which is precisely why this witness runs instead of merely compiling. !! AND THE ARM THAT DOES *NOT* RED IS RECORDED HERE BECAUSE THIS MANIFEST PREVIOUSLY CLAIMED IT DID -- a red-on-disable arm that cannot go red is a vacuous claim, so it is corrected rather than quietly deleted: retyping the DESCRIPTOR ROW alone (ctype.json `ptr<u8>` -> `arr<u8,256>`) changes NOTHING. MEASURED 2026-08-10 by EXERCISING it as a config-only mutation (no relink -- the corpus is read at runtime), mutant hash differing from the restored-byte-exact baseline and still parsing: compile rc=0 with ZERO diagnostics and exit 42 at BOTH debug AND release, i.e. the example kept PASSING. That is exactly what ctype.json's own comment predicts and what this manifest's own next sentence says -- realization hands over only the LIBRARY, so nothing compares a row's `kind` or signature against the declarator ([[D-FFI-SHIPPED-ROW-KIND-NOT-CROSSCHECKED-AGAINST-DECLARATOR]]) -- so the two statements contradicted each other and only running the arm decided which was right. The arm that IS load-bearing was exercised in the same run: un-shipping the row gives K_SymbolUndefined on this example AND on extern_data_addr_reject_pe, confirming the reject example's CODE pin is what keeps it failing for its own reason. bind data externs to thunk VAs or drop the got-indirect deref -> exit 4 or 0xC0000005 on the store. pe64-ONLY: `_mbcasemap` is a Windows CRT name; the elf/macho extern-DATA run witnesses are stdio_stream_objects (libc stdout/stderr/stdin via copy-relocation / Mach-O __got) and shipped_environ (POSIX `environ` via the elf strong `__environ`). The optimized arms prove the slot-deref address materialization survives the release pipelines.
